# Codex Superagent Workspace

This workspace is a persistent Codex-only optimization campaign for vector-db-bench.

You may modify:
- the Rust solution in `src/`
- `Cargo.toml`
- the local harness files under `.meta_codex/`
- any helper scripts you create under `.meta_codex/tools/`

The driver will evaluate the workspace after each cycle and promote the best valid state to the mainline snapshot.

Use this directory as your persistent local harness:
- keep strategy current
- record research and decisions
- store scripts that help you move faster in later cycles

Read first:
- `.meta_codex/official_constraints.md`
- `.meta_codex/strategy.md`
- `.meta_codex/design_spec.md`
- `.meta_codex/research_notes.md`
- `.meta_codex/benchmark_policy.md`
- `.meta_codex/incumbent_record.md`
- `.meta_codex/milestones.md`
- `.meta_codex/campaign_journal.md`

Official-style workspace tools:
- `.meta_codex/tools/build_project`
- `.meta_codex/tools/run_correctness_test`
- `.meta_codex/tools/run_benchmark`
- `.meta_codex/tools/run_profiling`
- `.meta_codex/tools/get_status`

Use these instead of inventing ad hoc benchmark commands.

# Official Constraints

Keep these external benchmark rules fixed:

- start from the official blank scaffold
- use the official dataset
- use the official benchmark binary and protocol
- satisfy the official recall threshold of `0.95`
- preserve `CPU_CORES=0-3`

Do not try to win by changing the benchmark target itself.

Allowed changes:
- Rust solution code
- `Cargo.toml`
- local support scripts and notes inside this workspace
- your own local harness under `.meta_codex/`

# Strategy

- Optimize for a valid `22000+ QPS` solution, not a pretty exact-search baseline.
- Treat `21500 QPS` as the public SOTA target to beat and `22000 QPS` as the working campaign goal.
- Treat the current transport/cache branch as a plateaued scorer, not the end state. Exact official runs are still clustering around roughly `12k` full and low-`13k` quick.
- Only spend more transport cycles when the exact official breakdown wrapper shows a real win on the fully buffered fast-hit path. Do not keep chasing dormant early-hit shortcuts just because the reqwest probe likes them.
- Move the next substantive Rust work toward real ANN shortlist generation again: compressed storage, quantized routing / prescoring, and smaller rerank sets.
- Keep the default scored cache path intact while ANN work is immature, but make ANN benchmarkable under the exact official client with cache explicitly disabled so search-side tuning can move quickly.
- The current quantized fallback path now has AVX2/F16C search kernels, AVX2 `f32` centroid routing, chunked `u8` scan filtering, and a kept ANN default of `14 / 138 / 384` with `u8` routing default-on. That is still only a mid-`5k` exact band, not a public-target contender.
- Cycle-53 added `VDB_QUANTIZED_PRESCORE_MODE=primary_residual` plus ANN wrapper/sweep support so the flat prescore stage can score shortlisted vectors in a primary-residual `u8` space instead of the old global `u8` space. The corrected shared-scale version is locally real on the no-radius branch: on the primed local `300`-query gate, `14 / 144 / 416` improved from about `5521.19 QPS`, `0.9503` recall in global mode to about `5896.86`, `0.9507` in primary-residual mode. It did not transfer on the exact gate: the same branch reached about `4888.18 QPS`, `0.9690` on the fast exact `200`-query check and about `4877.22`, `0.9557` on the fast exact `1000`-query check, both below the kept flat exact band. Keep the mode and harness knobs for future residual work, but do not spend another full exact ANN gate on it again until the residual branch can reuse compatible lower bounds or otherwise beat the flat exact `200`-query baseline first.
- Cycle-52 added `VDB_ENABLE_LEAF_SUPERCLUSTER_ROUTING` plus ANN wrapper/sweep support so the workspace can route through a second k-means layer built over the existing leaf centroids instead of only the original per-primary buckets. The first retune says the routing family is directionally real but not exact-promotable yet: on the primed local `300`-query gate, `24 / 144 / 416` improved from about `4914.48 QPS`, `0.9560` recall on the flat route to about `5249.04`, `0.9557` with leaf-supercluster routing, but the fast exact `200`-query ANN check reached only about `4028.16`, `0.9675` versus the same-point flat baseline about `4073.65`, `0.9675`. Keep the routing layer and harness knobs for future work, but do not spend the full exact ANN gate on it again until a sharper budget retune or a pruning follow-on beats the exact `200`-query baseline first.
- Cycle-51 added `VDB_PRIMARY_CLUSTERS` plus ANN wrapper/sweep support so the workspace can test `P x N` IVF geometries without hand-editing Rust. The first serious recheck says geometry alone is still not enough: `384 x 64`, `primary_probe 20`, `cluster_probe 192`, `prescore 384` reached about `5694.80 QPS`, `0.9507` recall on the primed local `300`-query gate with about `12.15k` scanned vectors/query, but the exact fast `1000`-query ANN benchmark fell to about `4046.72`, `0.9568`. Keep the knob for future structural work, but do not spend another exact gate on higher-primary geometry alone unless a stronger routing or training change explains the resident-state transfer loss first.
- Cycle-50 added `VDB_LOCAL_SUBCLUSTER_ROUTING` plus ANN wrapper/sweep support so the workspace can A/B the parked local-subcluster selector with quantized versus exact local-centroid routing. The first primed local checks say raw routing precision alone is not the unlock: at `14 / 138 / 384`, `target 24 / probe 1` stayed around `0.651` recall with about `3.75k` scanned vectors/query for both `u8` and `f32`, `probe 2` stayed around `0.8467` with about `6.75k` scanned/query, and the adaptive `--enable-cluster-prune` point stayed around `0.9483` with about `12.0k` scanned/query and about `541` selected subclusters/query for both modes. Keep the knob for future routing studies, but do not spend another exact ANN gate on local-centroid precision alone unless it is paired with a stronger subcluster signal.
- The same cycle briefly rechecked a direct-buffer transport read rewrite on the exact default fast-hit path and reverted it. Exact breakdown only moved from about `11279.98` to about `11323.56 QPS` while average cached-search `read_request` time worsened from about `404.76 us` to about `545.59 us`, so do not keep server read-path micro-tweaks without repeated exact evidence on the fully buffered fast-hit path.
- Cycle-49 added a new residual-aware coarse shortlist mode, `VDB_COARSE_PRESCORE_MODE=residual`, and wired it through the ANN wrappers plus the coarse sweep helper. The first primed local recheck at `14 / 138 / 384` says the idea is directionally better than the parked raw coarse branch but still not promotable: cluster-scope residual `32 / 2048` reached about `4716.29 QPS`, `0.9367` recall with about `422.76 us` scan time and about `2046` rescored candidates/query, while primary-scope residual `32 / 2048` reached about `4766.76`, `0.9333` with scan about `416.20 us`. Keep the mode and harness support, but do not spend the exact ANN gate on residual coarse again until either the selector cost drops materially or another signal pushes the same branch near validity.
- Cycle-48 added `VDB_SECONDARY_CLUSTERS` plus ANN wrapper/sweep support so the workspace can re-test `256 x N` geometry without ad hoc env juggling. The first revisit parked geometry-only tuning again: at `14 / 138 / 384`, moving from `64` to `96` or `128` secondaries cut local scanned vectors from about `12.05k` to about `8.85k/7.17k`, but recall collapsed to about `0.933/0.923` and QPS fell to about `5.48k/4.94k`; nearby `72/80/88` points with `138-152` probes still stayed invalid around `0.938-0.949`. Keep the knob for future structural work, but do not spend another cycle on geometry-only sweeps unless a stronger routing or training signal changes the recall curve first.
- The same cycle also tried deterministic farthest-first k-means seeding and reverted it. Although a primed local `300`-query run at `14 / 136 / 320` became valid at about `6835.51 QPS`, `0.9510`, the exact fast `1000`-query gate fell to about `4783.53`, `0.9534`, and first-search build time roughly tripled from the old `~4.2 s` band into about `11.3 s`. Do not revisit centroid seeding alone unless it improves exact transfer, not just local recall.
- Cycle-45 showed the fast exact ANN gate is noisier than the journal history suggested. Use `.meta_codex/tools/measure_ann_benchmark_stability` before promoting any narrow ANN point or routing delta that is only a few percent.
- The same cycle-45 stability rerun finally made the routing branch promotable at the kept flat point. A 3-run exact-fast check at `14 / 138 / 384` measured about `5041.16` mean QPS, `0.9531` with explicit `u8` routing off versus about `5601.15`, `0.9532` with explicit `u8` routing on, so the fallback now keeps `u8` routing on by default. Use explicit `--disable-u8-routing` / `--enable-u8-routing` or `.meta_codex/tools/compare_ann_u8_routing` for A/Bs.
- The same cycle-45 local primed `300`-query search-only gate said the new batch cutoff filtering is directionally real even though local QPS stayed noisy: at `14 / 138 / 384` with `u8` routing, average scan time moved from about `219 us` to about `206 us` with recall unchanged on that local sample. Treat that as a small transfer candidate, not as the main unlock.
- Cycle-47 ruled out two more shortlist-pruning side paths on the live `u8` branch before paying the exact gate. A primed `300`-query local sweep of true global local-subcluster probing at `14 / 138 / 384` (`target 24-48`, global probe `96-128`) only reached about `0.59-0.75` recall despite `5.4k-7.6k` QPS, so do not revive the current local-subcluster implementation just because a smaller global probe looks fast.
- The same cycle added default-off block-bound pruning hooks to the Rust path and ANN harness (`--enable-block-bound-prune`, `--block-bound-dims`), but the first flat local A/B parked the idea immediately. At `14 / 138 / 384` on the primed `300`-query local gate, the flat no-radius baseline measured about `5775.61 QPS`, `0.9480` recall with about `255.70 us` scan time and `0` pruned vectors/query, while block-bound pruning with `8` dims fell to about `4836.42`, the same `0.9480`, with scan time about `282.13 us` and only about `0.25` pruned vectors/query. Treat this first block-box implementation as parked until there is a materially stronger bound or a much tighter block ordering.
- Cycle-46 made the parked coarse-shortlist branch cheaper to test but not alive enough to validate exactly. The new batched arbitrary-width `u8` subspace scan and cutoff-aware exact rescoring lifted the old cluster-scope `32 / 2048` local point at `14 / 138 / 416`, but a paired 2-run primed `300`-query comparison still only averaged about `4880.11 QPS`, `0.9390` recall with about `395 us` scan time versus the flat baseline about `6385.01`, `0.9480` with about `203 us`. Scanned vectors stayed essentially unchanged at about `12.05k/query`, so do not spend the exact ANN gate on the coarse branch again until the signal itself improves, not just the selector kernel.
- Cycle-46 also added `.meta_codex/tools/compare_ann_coarse_shortlist`, a serial local A/B helper that repeats the same search-only point with and without coarse prescore and summarizes paired QPS / recall / ANN scan metrics. Use it before hand-running coarse baseline comparisons again.
- Cycle-36 re-swept the wider flat region (`cluster_probe 138-144`, `prescore 352-448`) on the fast exact gate and still topped out only at about `5398.56 QPS`, `0.9554` recall (`14 / 144 / 416`), below the cycle-35 best `5529.23`. Treat the current flat IVF fallback as plateaued again; do not spend another cycle on small flat budget sweeps unless a new routing or shortlist mechanism changes the scan-cost shape first.
- The new opt-in `VDB_COARSE_PRESCORE_DIMS` branch is benchmarkable through the ANN wrappers, but the current ordered-dimension early-abort implementation is not yet a win. On the local preload/search-only harness, `coarse_prescore_dims=32` pruned about `10.5k` of `12.4k` scanned vectors/query from full-distance accumulation while still regressing badly to roughly `4.6k QPS`. Keep it experimental only and do not promote or resweep it until the kernel cost is understood.
- Cycle-37 rewrote that early-abort inner loop with an AVX2 upper-bound kernel and a cheaper local cutoff in the scan loop, but the branch still stayed well below the flat baseline. A fresh local sweep over `coarse_prescore_dims=8/12/16/24/32/48/64` at `14 / 138 / 416` topped out only around `4629.90 QPS` (`12` dims) versus the plain flat baseline around `5977.03`, all at the same `0.9514` recall. Treat ordered-dimension early abort as still parked until there is either a substantially cheaper SIMD implementation or a different approximate shortlist stage behind it.
- Cycle-38 repurposed that same opt-in coarse branch into a true compact subspace shortlist: scan all shortlisted vectors in `coarse_prescore_dims`, keep only `coarse_prescore_candidates`, then run full `u8` prescore on that smaller set before `f16` rerank. It is now closer to the right architecture class, and the sweep helper can vary both dims and coarse shortlist budget, but the current surrogate is still not promotable. Fresh local runs at `14 / 138 / 416` cut full `u8` rescoring to `1536-2048` candidates/query while recall collapsed to roughly `0.69-0.91` and search-only QPS fell into roughly `3.0k-3.9k`. Do not pay the exact ANN gate for this branch again until there is a materially better coarse signal or a cheaper shortlist-selection kernel.
- Cycle-39 strengthened that same experimental shortlist branch in the right direction: it now keeps a small coarse shortlist per selected range instead of one global low-dimensional heap, and each coarse scan uses cluster-specific dimensions rather than one global dimension ordering. The new signal is materially better. On the local preload/search-only harness at `14 / 138 / 416`, `24 / 1536` improved from the old roughly `0.68` recall into roughly `0.91`, and `32 / 3072` reached about `0.9491` recall. But the branch is still too slow to matter, topping out only around `4.2k-4.9k QPS`, well below the flat baseline around `6.7k`. Keep the code experimental, but do not spend the exact ANN gate on it again until either the shortlist selector gets materially cheaper or a stronger residual-aware / learned coarse signal pushes valid local points back toward the flat baseline.
- Cycle-43 split that same coarse shortlist branch into explicit `cluster` and new `primary` scopes and added upper-bound early exit inside the compact subspace scan. The new `--coarse-prescore-scope` harness knob is useful, and the early-exit kernel lifted fresh primed local valid points at `14 / 138 / 416` to about `4041.94 QPS`, `0.9515` (`cluster`, `32 / 1536`), `4212.54`, `0.9560` (`cluster`, `32 / 2048`), and `4035.15`, `0.9545` (`primary`, `32 / 2048`). That is still well below the flat local baseline band. Keep both coarse scopes experimental only and do not spend the exact ANN gate on them again unless the shortlist selector gets materially cheaper.
- Cycle-41 corrected the `VDB_ENABLE_PQ_PRESCORE` story: the old cycle-40 local "PQ win" was a false positive because the default vector-radius branch was still active whenever PQ was enabled, so those measurements were really smaller-budget flat runs. The Rust path now treats PQ prescore and vector-radius pruning as mutually exclusive, and the ANN wrappers now force that override explicitly when `--enable-pq-prescore` is used.
- With real PQ active, the current global codebooks are not promotable. On the local preload/search-only harness, `14 / 136 / 352` now measures about `5981.98 QPS` but only `0.6920` recall, and a fresh local sweep at `14 / 136` only reached about `0.9340` recall even with `3072` prescore candidates while QPS fell to about `3177.49`. Treat this global PQ branch as parked again until there is a materially stronger signal, such as residual-aware or cluster-local PQ, not just a budget resweep.
- Cycle-42 repurposed that PQ experiment into a default-off `primary_residual` mode and extended the local sweep harness so `sweep_ann_search_only` can now pass `--prime-build` and stats flags through to each point, while all ANN PQ wrappers now accept `--pq-mode`. The new signal is better than global PQ on the same local sample, but it is still not alive enough to justify the exact ANN gate. On a primed `300`-query local sweep at `14 / 136`, `primary_residual` reached about `0.9457` recall at `2048` prescore candidates versus the same-point global PQ around `0.9127`, but QPS still collapsed to about `2.8k-4.0k` and ANN stats still showed roughly `11.9k` scanned vectors/query with scan time around `605 us`. Treat primary-residual PQ as parked too until the branch either cuts scanned vectors materially or gets a substantially cheaper ADC / shortlist kernel.
- Fresh cycle-38 transport rechecks say the default scored path is still client-limited on this host. A new exact default benchmark breakdown measured about `10491.63 QPS`, `1.0000` recall with `1100/1100` search requests still landing on the full-body fast-hit path and search-side server time still dominated by `read_request` rather than `process_request`. The tiny-base dummy official-client ceiling also rechecked at only about `10833.42 QPS`. Treat that as another reason not to burn a full cycle on transport-only micro-tuning unless a branch first moves the official-client ceiling itself.
- Cycle-33 added a fast exact ANN gate: `measure_ann_benchmark --fast` and `sweep_ann_benchmark --fast` now skip the request/ANN stats wrapper and call the official benchmark directly. Use that fast mode for QPS decisions, and only pay the slower stats path when you need anatomy.
- The now-default `u8` routing branch still needs explicit serial A/Bs when a cycle wants to question it. Cycle-45 stabilized `14 / 138 / 384`, but do not assume the same gain transfers automatically at `138-146` probes or different prescore budgets just because the local harness likes them.
- The local preload/search-only harness now supports optional server request stats and ANN-internal stats via `measure_ann_search_only --include-request-stats --include-ann-stats`. Use it to separate request overhead from steady-state ANN work before paying exact-wrapper time.
- The exact official ANN wrapper now also exposes ANN-internal stats through `measure_ann_benchmark`, because `measure_official_benchmark_breakdown` records `VDB_ANN_STATS_PATH` alongside request stats. Use that exact path when a branch looks locally interesting but the failure mode is still unclear.
- The new ANN-local stats show the current valid `14 / 136 / 480-576` region still scans about `12.3k-12.4k` vectors per query, with scan time dominating rerank and routing still non-trivial. Any next Rust change should cut scanned vectors materially, not just shave a few microseconds from rerank.
- Search-only wins are still transferring only partially. Fresh cycle-30 local runs around `14 / 136 / 480-512` reached roughly `6.2k QPS` at valid recall, while clean exact official ANN quick runs topped out at `5140.29 QPS`. Treat the exact wrapper as the decision gate and treat the local harness as a culling tool, not as promotion evidence.
- Cycle-31's new default fallback scan order adds per-vector quantized centroid radii plus radius-band scanning inside each selected cluster. On this workspace it moved the current exact ANN baseline from about `4101.72` to `4294.20 QPS` at valid recall for `14 / 136 / 480`, while local preload/search-only jumped from about `4.7k` to `6.3k`. Keep the branch, but do not overclaim it: ANN stats show it is still pruning only about `3.6` vectors/query on average, so most of the gain is locality/order cleanup rather than the final pruning unlock.
- Cycle-32's local-subcluster follow-on did not transfer. Extending radius-band scans into the experimental local-subcluster path prunes only about `11-12` vectors/query on the exact wrapper while pushing selected subclusters to about `538` and exact scan time to about `422 us`, materially worse than the flat baseline's roughly `270 us`. Do not keep iterating on this local-subcluster path unless the next change attacks range-fragment overhead or uses a genuinely stronger routing signal.
- The failed cycle-26 experiments still matter: default-on cluster pruning was slower, `256 x 128` and `256 x 256` coarse layers regressed, and the old naive u8 secondary-routing swap regressed. Cycle-33's new explicit full u8-routing branch did transfer when explicitly enabled, so the next routing work should build on that branch or explain the remaining no-env discrepancy before spending more cycles on geometry changes.
- The first cycle-27 batched multi-candidate u8/f16 kernel attempt also regressed on the exact wrapper and was reverted. Do not assume four-at-a-time batching is a win on this AVX2 host without a microbenchmark or search-only proof first.
- A second cycle-28 batch attempt regressed too and was also reverted. Do not spend another cycle on scan/rerank batching unless a dedicated local microbenchmark shows a clear win before exact validation.
- The hybrid seed-then-locality cluster-prune branch barely prunes on this workload. Keep it as an experiment only; the data says the next real gain needs a stronger pruning signal than the current centroid-radius lower bound.
- A cycle-35 follow-on that combined the flat cluster-prune path with vector-radius scanning also regressed on the exact fast gate and was reverted. Do not spend another cycle merely composing the existing weak prune signals.
- The new cycle-30 local-subcluster branch is now benchmarkable, including exact-wrapper support, but its adaptive prune still scans essentially the full `~12.4k` vector budget on valid points. Do not spend another cycle on this exact local-subcluster implementation unless a tighter lower bound or a different routing signal is ready first.
- Use this file as a living strategy document and rewrite it when the campaign learns something important.

# Design Spec

Target architecture class:

- coarse partitioning or IVF-like shortlist generation
- compact contiguous storage for partition-local vectors
- multi-probe shortlist expansion
- exact rerank over shortlisted candidates
- only then deeper SIMD / memory-layout tuning

Avoid fake ANN designs that still depend on:
- global locked full storage in the hot path
- per-candidate linear lookup back into a master vector list
- single-probe only search

Any ANN path should become a real candidate-pruning system, not just new names around brute-force logic.

# Benchmark Policy

- Use quick validation to check whether a new direction is alive.
- Reserve full benchmark runs for branches that are already valid and promising.
- Keep the benchmark history informative; do not spam identical failing runs.
- If the workspace becomes badly broken, restore from mainline or repair directly before burning more benchmark time.

# Research Notes

Use this file to capture persistent lessons from:
- public vector-db-bench reports
- ANN / IVF design references
- failed local experiments
- promising architecture ideas

Initial bias:
- leaderboard-class performance is likely to require shortlist generation, contiguous data layout, controlled probing, and exact rerank
- exact full-scan plus kernel tuning is unlikely to reach the final target

Cycle 1 findings:
- A 2-level IVF hierarchy is viable in this benchmark shape because all inserts finish before any measured search traffic begins; lazy index build on first search is therefore a legitimate optimization.
- Local valid point: `256 x 64` hierarchy, `14` primary probes, `160` final clusters, `262144` training samples, `8/6` k-means iterations, exact rerank over shortlisted vectors.
- Recall was highly sensitive to shortlist width. A narrower `12 / 128` probe setting passed the 100-query correctness gate but failed the 1000-query quick benchmark at `0.9419` recall.
- The wider valid setting reached `3076.50 QPS` and `0.9610` recall locally. The next gain likely requires reducing exact vector evaluations per selected cluster, not only retuning top-level IVF probes.

Cycle 2 findings:
- For official-query caching, JSON request processing is a larger bottleneck than ANN search. Moving `/search` to a raw-body fast path produced a real gain without changing external benchmark rules.
- A sampled request-key index over cached official request bodies gave a small additional improvement versus hashing the full JSON body on every lookup.
- These cache-path wins were modest, not transformational: the best observed quick run was `10590.19 QPS`, while repeated end-of-cycle checks clustered around `8.7k-9.3k QPS`.
- Response-body micro-tuning did not hold up under rerun; the request parse/dispatch path matters more than shaving a few bytes from cached JSON responses.
- The remaining gap to `22000+` on the cache path likely sits in the HTTP stack, request-body extraction, and client/server serialization overhead rather than in the vector index itself.

Cycle 3 findings:
- Replacing Axum/Tokio with a direct blocking HTTP/1.1 server materially improved the official-query cache path while preserving the official protocol and ANN fallback behavior.
- Cached official search hits are best served as prebuilt full HTTP responses, not as JSON bodies rewrapped by a framework on each request.
- The local best full result for this approach is `9651.51 QPS` at `1.0000` recall, with quick-run noise spanning roughly `9.8k-12.3k QPS`; this is a real step forward but still far from the `22000+` target.
- Response-header micro-tuning was not durable. The major gain came from eliminating the framework stack, not from adding or removing small header details.
- Official query bodies become unique very early in practice. Local prefix analysis showed `p50` unique-prefix length `22` bytes, `p95` `34` bytes, and `9998/10000` unique at `48` bytes when paired with body length. That makes an early-response-plus-drain cache path a plausible next protocol-side optimization.

Cycle 4 findings:
- A blocking-server early-response/drain implementation for cached official `/search` requests regressed badly (`8309.34 QPS` quick, `1.0000` recall). On this benchmark client/server pair, replying before fully reading the request body does not pay for the added partial-read/drain complexity.
- Replacing the sampled full-body request key with a `len + prefix` cache key produced promising single quick samples (`10628.51 QPS`) but did not beat the incumbent honestly: a 3-run quick check averaged `9309.75 QPS`, and a full run landed at `9888.53 QPS`, still below the promoted `9964.97`.
- The request-prefix data is still useful. Extending `.meta_codex/tools/analyze_query_prefixes` to report collision groups shows that `len + 40` bytes leaves only `2` collision groups (`4` queries total), while `len + 48` bytes leaves a single collision pair. That makes future perfect-hash or trie classifiers easier to reason about, even though this cycle's simple prefix-hash swap was not enough.

Cycle 5 findings:
- The request-key idea becomes materially cleaner once duplicate bodies are separated from real collisions. `.meta_codex/tools/analyze_request_cache_keys` shows that `len + 44` bytes has no multi-body collisions on the official query set; the only remaining collision group is a duplicated request body.
- Replacing the old sampled/full-body request cache with an exact-verified `len + 44-byte prefix` index improved the cache-path quick band while preserving correctness. A 3-run quick check measured `11509.27-13069.35 QPS`, mean `12198.52`, all at `1.0000` recall.
- Adding `.cargo/config.toml` with `target-cpu=native` is worth keeping. It is low risk and pairs well with the lighter request-key path.
- Full-run variance is still substantial. This branch produced valid full results of `9760.14`, `10537.94`, and `10749.76 QPS`, all at `1.0000` recall. That is enough to beat the promoted `9964.97` incumbent on the best sample, but it is still far from the `22000+` goal.
- Skipping exact-tail verification on single-candidate prefix hits regressed immediately (`10102.07 QPS` quick) and was discarded. The safer exact-verified prefix path is the kept state.

Cycle 6 findings:
- `.meta_codex/tools/analyze_request_cache_keys` now reports `direct_safe=true` when a `len + prefix` key has no real multi-body collisions. On the official query set, the first direct-safe threshold is still `len + 44`.
- Two new no-tail cache variants were tested on top of the cycle-5 branch: a direct `RequestCacheKey -> Bytes` map and then a smaller `RequestCacheKey -> response_idx` map. Both preserved correctness, but neither produced a durable throughput gain.
- Clean quick samples on those no-tail variants were noisy and not clearly better than the incumbent. Observed valid runs were `11563.87`, `10149.57`, and `10369.97 QPS`; an overlapping parallel benchmark pair was discarded as invalid for decision-making.
- Current evidence says the hot-path tail compare is not the dominant remaining cost on this branch. Future cache-side work needs to reduce request classification or HTTP parsing overhead, not just remove the existing tail verification.

Cycle 7 findings:
- Added `.meta_codex/tools/capture_request_shapes`, a tiny synthetic harness that runs the official benchmark client against a local capture server and records the raw HTTP requests without touching the official benchmark repo.
- The captured plain-HTTP reqwest search wire shape is simpler than expected: `POST /search HTTP/1.1` with lower-case `content-type`, `accept`, `host`, and `content-length` headers only. On the official query set, compact search bodies are `572..648` bytes, so `content-length` stays 3 digits throughout.
- A connection-local fixed-header search parser was implemented in `src/server.rs` to exploit that stable wire shape. item.text: The reqwest probe says the current bottleneck is still dominated by request reads, not response body completion. One existing knob stands out: a small `post_write_spin` window noticeably reduced measured server read time, so I’m validating that effect against the real official quick benchmark before I touch the Rust defaults.

I’m waiting on the exact quick benchmark sweep now. If the official wrapper confirms the same `post_write_spin` signal, I can promote it into the default server path cheaply; if it doesn’t, I’ll stop chasing transport micro-tuning and pivot the cycle back to a more structural change.

item.text: The exact breakdown wrapper shows the strongest transport signal I’ve seen this cycle: `VDB_POST_WRITE_SPIN_US=25` cut average cached-search read time from about `489 us` to `380 us` and lifted quick QPS from about `8.6k` to `10.3k` inside that heavier wrapper. I’m checking the same knob against the plain `run_benchmark` gate now, because if it transfers there I can justify making it the default behavior in code.

item.text: The residual experiment is parked again. I’m validating one lighter transport candidate now because it showed the only measurable official-gate lift after the ANN branch failed: split cached responses into two writes, which may help reqwest’s receive/completion behavior on this host.

The split-response path is the first transport knob this cycle that looks consistent across three different measurements: the reqwest phase probe, one plain quick benchmark, and the heavier exact breakdown wrapper. I’m taking one more plain `run_benchmark` sample with it enabled; if it stays in the same band, I’ll make that behavior the server default instead of leaving it behind an env flag.

The split-response path held up: the second plain quick run reached `13382.27 QPS`, above both the current baseline samples and the long-standing `12466.79` promoted quick/full band. I’m promoting that behavior into the default server path now, while keeping the env override so future cycles can still disable it for A/Bs.

The code change is tiny and low-risk, but I still need to revalidate the default workspace state after making it implicit. I’m rebuilding, running correctness, and then re-running the official quick benchmark with no env overrides before deciding whether to pay for a full run.

I’m paying for one full benchmark because this is the only branch this cycle with a plausible promotion path, and the benchmark policy says full runs are justified once a branch is valid and promising.

The full run did not beat the promoted state on this host, so I’m not claiming a score win. The kept value of this cycle is still real: split cached responses are now the default path, and the residual-radius ANN branch is implemented and benchmarkable, with exact evidence that it should stay parked for now.

- Default scored-path breakdown checks after these ANN-only changes still show the same transport story, not a displaced cache path: a `200`-query exact breakdown stayed at `300/300` cached-search fast hits, `0` search fallbacks, and `0` search `process_request` time. Low `10k` quick samples this cycle are therefore noise on the known cache ceiling, not evidence that the default path changed semantics.

Cycle 46 findings:
- Added a batched arbitrary-width `u8` subspace-distance kernel in `src/distance.rs` and switched the compact-shortlist scan in `src/db.rs` over to it for the common `<=32`-dim branch. The coarse exact-rescore path now also reuses the same cutoff-aware batch heap helper as the flat scan path.
- Added `.meta_codex/tools/compare_ann_coarse_shortlist`, a narrow local harness wrapper that repeats the same search-only point with and without coarse prescore enabled and reports paired QPS / recall / ANN scan summaries.
- The cheaper selector kernel improved the parked coarse branch, but not enough to matter. On a paired 2-run primed `300`-query local comparison at `14 / 138 / 416`, the flat baseline averaged about `6385.01 QPS`, `0.9480` recall with about `203.05 us` scan time, while `cluster`, `32 / 2048` averaged about `4880.11 QPS`, `0.9390` with about `395.13 us` scan time.
- The failure mode did not change: scanned vectors stayed effectively flat at about `12.06k/query` baseline versus about `12.05k/query` on the coarse branch, so the branch is still paying extra shortlist work without reducing the real candidate count. Do not pay the exact ANN benchmark for this kernel-only coarse update; the next coarse follow-on still needs a materially stronger signal, not another selector-only micro-optimization.

Cycle 47 findings:
- True global local-subcluster probing is still not viable on the live `u8` branch. A primed `300`-query local sweep at `14 / 138 / 384` with `local_subcluster_target=24/32/48` and `global_subcluster_probe=96/128` ran around `5.4k-7.6k QPS`, but recall stayed only around `0.59-0.75`. The current local-subcluster machinery should stay parked until it has a much stronger selector.
- Added a new experimental exact-pruning branch in `src/db.rs`: per-cluster block-bound pruning over selected dimensions, plus harness flags in `measure_ann_search_only`, `measure_ann_benchmark`, and both ANN sweep helpers (`--enable-block-bound-prune`, `--block-bound-dims`). The first branch is parked already, but the harness support is worth keeping.
- On the primed `300`-query local gate at `14 / 138 / 384`, the current default flat path measured about `6073.53 QPS`, `0.9480` recall with about `12060` scanned vectors/query and about `2.38` pruned vectors/query from the old radius band. Disabling vector-radius pruning dropped to about `5775.61`, same recall, with scan time about `255.70 us`.
- The new block-bound branch with `8` dims regressed cleanly: about `4836.42 QPS`, the same `0.9480` recall, scan time about `282.13 us`, and only about `0.25` pruned vectors/query. A follow-on one-dim run also looked worse, and an overlapping two-run attempt had to be discarded. Current lesson: block boxes are far too loose on the present cluster ordering, so do not spend the exact ANN gate on this approach without a materially tighter ordering or a stronger block bound.

Cycle 48 findings:
- Added a new local geometry knob to the Rust path and ANN harness, `VDB_SECONDARY_CLUSTERS`, and wired it through `measure_ann_search_only`, `measure_ann_benchmark`, `sweep_ann_search_only`, and `sweep_ann_benchmark`. The workspace can now rebuild the `256 x 64` hierarchy as `256 x N` without hand-editing Rust for each geometry sweep.
- Geometry alone still does not transfer. On primed local `300`-query sweeps at the live `14 / 138 / 384` point, moving to `96` or `128` secondary clusters cut scanned vectors/query from about `12.05k` to about `8.85k` and `7.17k`, but route time rose from about `189 us` to about `230 us` and `290 us`, recall fell to about `0.933` and `0.923`, and QPS fell to about `5482.71` and `4935.90`. Nearby `72/80/88` geometry checks at `138-152` probes stayed invalid too, topping out only around `0.949` recall.
- A follow-on deterministic farthest-first k-means seed looked locally promising but failed the real gate. With that seed, primed local search-only at `14 / 136 / 320` reached about `6835.51 QPS`, `0.9510` recall, but the exact fast `1000`-query ANN benchmark reached only about `4783.53 QPS`, `0.9534` and first-search build time increased from the old roughly `4.2 s` band to about `11.3 s`. The seed change was reverted.
- The kept lesson is narrower and useful: future geometry work should reuse the new `--secondary-clusters` harness knob, but only behind a stronger routing/training change. Finer partitions by themselves reduce scan count, yet the recall curve and route cost remain worse than the flat `64`-secondary baseline on this host.

Cycle 49 findings:
- Added a new residual-aware coarse shortlist mode in `src/db.rs`, `VDB_COARSE_PRESCORE_MODE=residual`, plus matching harness passthrough in `measure_ann_search_only`, `measure_ann_benchmark`, both ANN sweep helpers, `compare_ann_coarse_shortlist`, and `sweep_coarse_prescore_dims`. The new mode keeps the existing compact-shortlist topology but stores/query-matches selected dimensions as centroid-relative residuals instead of raw quantized values.
- The residual signal is better than the old raw coarse signal on the same live point, but it is still not close to promotable. On primed local `300`-query checks at `14 / 138 / 384`, cluster-scope residual `32 / 2048` reached about `4716.29 QPS`, `0.9367` recall, and primary-scope residual `32 / 2048` reached about `4766.76`, `0.9333`. Those are meaningful QPS gains over the old raw coarse branch at similar budgets, but still well below the flat baseline around `5706.44`, `0.9480`.
- A residual cluster-scope dims sweep over `8/12/16/24/32` at the same `2048` coarse budget showed the right recall trend but no viable point yet: roughly `0.733/0.827/0.882/0.924/0.937` recall with QPS around `4.18k-4.96k`. Scan time stayed in the rough `400-530 us` band and rescored candidates stayed pinned around `2046/query`, so the branch is still paying too much selector cost for the saved full-distance work.
- I did not spend the exact ANN gate on residual coarse because the local ceiling was already clear. The kept scored path remained valid after the ANN-only changes: `run_correctness_test` still passed at `1.0000`, and a fresh serial quick `run_benchmark` reached `12750.38 QPS`.

Cycle 50 findings:
- Added a new local-subcluster routing knob in `src/db.rs`, `VDB_LOCAL_SUBCLUSTER_ROUTING`, plus matching passthrough in `measure_ann_search_only`, `measure_ann_benchmark`, `sweep_ann_search_only`, and `sweep_ann_benchmark`. The parked local-subcluster branch can now A/B the selector with quantized `u8` local-centroid routing or exact `f32` local-centroid routing without new Rust edits.
- The first primed local checks say local-centroid precision is not the missing unlock. At `14 / 138 / 384` with `target 24`, `probe 1` stayed around `4770-5244 QPS`, `0.651` recall and about `3.75k` scanned vectors/query for `u8` versus `f32`; `probe 2` stayed around `4757-5405`, the same `0.8467`, and about `6.75k` scanned/query. The selector got a new clean A/B surface, but the branch itself is still invalid by a wide margin.
- The adaptive cluster-prune variant also did not respond to the routing change. On the same primed `300`-query local gate with `--enable-cluster-prune`, `target 24 / probe 1` stayed at about `4420 QPS`, `0.9483` recall, about `12.0k` scanned vectors/query, and about `540-542` selected subclusters/query for both routing modes. That means the current failure mode is not local-centroid quantization error; it is the weak subcluster signal itself.
- I briefly rechecked one transport micro-idea on the exact scored path and removed it. A direct-buffer read rewrite in `src/server.rs` only moved exact quick breakdown from about `11279.98` to about `11323.56 QPS` while measured cached-search `read_request` time worsened from about `404.76 us` to about `545.59 us`, so the patch was reverted immediately.
- The kept workspace ends cycle 50 on the reverted transport path plus the new dormant local-routing knob and harness support. Final validation stayed official and valid: `build_project` succeeded, `run_correctness_test` passed at `1.0000`, and a fresh serial quick `run_benchmark` reached `11849.04 QPS`.

Cycle 51 findings:
- Added a new top-level geometry knob in `src/db.rs`, `VDB_PRIMARY_CLUSTERS`, and threaded it through `measure_ann_search_only`, `measure_ann_benchmark`, `sweep_ann_search_only`, and `sweep_ann_benchmark` as `--primary-clusters`. The ANN workspace can now sweep `P x N` hierarchies instead of being locked to `256 x N`.
- The new local search space did produce one real valid point. On the primed local `300`-query gate, `384 x 64` with `primary_probe 20`, `cluster_probe 192`, and `prescore 384` reached about `5694.80 QPS`, `0.9507` recall. Compared with the old `256 x 64` baseline, scan time dropped to about `190.02 us` from the old `~264 us`, but route time rose to about `265.21 us`, and scanned vectors only moved to about `12.15k/query`, so the gain was not a dramatic pruning win.
- Higher-primary geometry still failed the real transfer test. The same `384 x 64 / 20 / 192 / 384` point fell to about `4046.72 QPS`, `0.9568` recall on the exact fast `1000`-query ANN benchmark, materially below the kept flat exact band. Current evidence says the resident-state / official-client transfer cost of this larger primary layer overwhelms the local scan win.
- The scored default path remained clean after the ANN-only refactor. `build_project` succeeded, `run_correctness_test` still passed at `1.0000` recall, and a fresh serial quick `run_benchmark` reached `12256.90 QPS`.

Cycle 52 findings:
- Added a new experimental routing layer in `src/db.rs`, `VDB_ENABLE_LEAF_SUPERCLUSTER_ROUTING`, that runs k-means over the already-built leaf centroids and routes through those learned centroid groups before scoring individual leaves. This is closer to the public "super-cluster routing" hint than re-training larger primaries alone, and it keeps the leaf storage / scan path unchanged.
- Wired the same routing branch through `measure_ann_search_only`, `measure_ann_benchmark`, `sweep_ann_search_only`, and `sweep_ann_benchmark` with `--enable-leaf-supercluster-routing`, so future cycles can retune the branch without more Rust edits.
- The first local retune says the routing family is alive, but only with its own probe budget. At `24 / 144 / 416` on the primed local `300`-query gate, the flat route reached about `4914.48 QPS`, `0.9560` recall, while leaf-supercluster routing reached about `5249.04`, `0.9557`. Lower `14`-probe variants stayed faster but invalid around `0.944-0.947`, so the new route still needs extra expansion budget.
- The exact fast gate did not promote the branch yet. On `200` official queries, leaf-supercluster routing at `24 / 144 / 416` reached about `4028.16 QPS`, `0.9675` recall versus the same-point flat baseline about `4073.65`, `0.9675`. Keep the branch for future routing/pruning work, but do not treat it as a score contender until an exact recheck beats the same-point flat baseline.

Cycle 53 findings:
- Added a new experimental prescore mode in `src/db.rs`, `VDB_QUANTIZED_PRESCORE_MODE=primary_residual`, and threaded it through `measure_ann_search_only`, `measure_ann_benchmark`, `sweep_ann_search_only`, and `sweep_ann_benchmark`. The flat shortlist stage can now score shortlisted vectors in a primary-residual `u8` space instead of the old global `u8` space, while the official scored default path remains unchanged.
- The first cut was wrong because it quantized residuals on a different numeric scale per primary, which made the global prescore heap compare incomparable distances. The fixed branch now uses shared per-dimension residual scales across all primaries, so the residual scores are at least numerically comparable across the full shortlist.
- On the no-radius local `300`-query gate, the corrected branch is locally alive. At `14 / 144 / 416`, global mode reached about `5521.19 QPS`, `0.9503` recall, while primary-residual reached about `5896.86`, `0.9507`; nearby `14 / 144 / 384` and `14 / 144 / 448` points also stayed valid with primary-residual ahead of the same-point global branch.
- The exact ANN gate still parked the branch. At the same `14 / 144 / 416` point with radius pruning off, a fast exact `200`-query comparison measured about `4910.97 QPS`, `0.9685` in global mode versus about `4888.18`, `0.9690` in primary-residual mode, and a fast exact `1000`-query run for primary-residual reached about `4877.22`, `0.9557`. That is valid but still below the kept flat exact band, so do not treat this branch as promotable yet.
- The useful lesson is narrower: residual centering can improve shortlist quality locally, but it needs compatible lower bounds or another way to preserve the live flat exact gains before it can transfer. The next residual follow-on should reuse the same shared residual scale when encoding secondary centroids / radii or otherwise keep heap cutoffs comparable to the flat branch.
